- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply mean reversion to prior 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early periods (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; cap early forecast values at 1–2% below recent 10-day high.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 0.7×bullish + 0.3×bearish) to adjust forecast baseline.
